definitions.explanation: Texts written in classical Chinese, or the Japanese academic discipline of reading and interpreting such texts using special reading marks. A required subject in Japanese high school education.

examples.japanese: {高校|こうこう}で{漢文|かんぶん}を{習|なら}った。
examples.english: I studied kanbun in high school.

examples.japanese: {漢文|かんぶん}の{読|よ}み{下|くだ}しは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: Reading kanbun in Japanese word order is difficult.
examples.notes: {読|よ}み{下|くだ}し refers to the technique of reading classical Chinese texts in Japanese grammatical order.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{古典|こてん}{文学|ぶんがく}を{深|ふか}く{理解|りかい}するには、{漢文|かんぶん}の{知識|ちしき}が{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: Knowledge of kanbun is essential for a deep understanding of Japanese classical literature.

notes:
USAGE:
{漢文|かんぶん} is a core subject in Japanese high school education alongside {古文|こぶん} (classical Japanese). Students learn to read classical Chinese texts using {返|かえ}り{点|てん} (return marks) and {送|おく}りがな that indicate Japanese word order. Many famous passages from Chinese classics like the Analerta of Confucius and Tang poetry are studied.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {漢文|かんぶん}の{授業|じゅぎょう}: kanbun class
- {漢文|かんぶん}の{読|よ}み{下|くだ}し: reading kanbun in Japanese order
- {漢文|かんぶん}{訓読|くんどく}: Japanese reading of classical Chinese
- {返|かえ}り{点|てん}: return marks (used in kanbun)
